llm_input:
Synopsis:
Druids hold court to determine whether or not to lock up a tiefling child for stealing their precious artifact. If you fail to stop them, the child tries to run and is attacked by their guardian snakes.Sagha the druid leader is the main player in this scene. She is machiavellian, and flips to evil should the snakes attack the child.

Cluster Contexts:
- DEN_ShadowDruid_SnakesCourt.json: The circle has convened a druidic "court" where a tiefling child is accused of stealing a valuable grove artifact and stands pleading while a guardian snake coils at her side. Earlier you exposed Kagha as a Shadow Druid and a Cloakwood contingent led by Olodan has just arrived, their presence visibly warping grove creatures into shadow-druids and pressing the circle to purge "tainted" elements. Kagha is a trusted leader who is visibly torn and may be persuadable, but she’s already leaning toward harsh measures — calling the child a thief/poison and threatening imprisonment or exile — while Rath argues in the child’s defense. If you fail to intervene, the child will try to flee and the guardian snakes will attack; the scene can escalate into a choice to sway Kagha or to fight Olodan and his transformed druids.
- DEN_ShadowDruid_Leader.json: Player speaks with Kagha, the secret Shadow druid. Various paths of conversation reflect whether Kagha's actions led to a child's death or not. She may be neutral/Machiavellian or pure evil, depending.
- DEN_ShadowDruid_AD_LeaderPersuaded.json: Plays ONLY if Rath died in the combat against the Shadow Druids! If Rath is alive, He and Kagha have an AD together instead. In all cases, Kagha is mourning, shocked and repentant at what she has done.
- DEN_ShadowDruid_Denouncing.json: You have just exposed Kagha as a Shadow Druid, and as you confront her the rats in the grove visibly shift into shadow-druids — a Cloakwood contingent led by the sleazy, slobbering Olodan has arrived and openly welcomes the circle into their fold. Olodan accuses Halsin and the circle of letting "untouchables" corrupt the grove and immediately orders Kagha to purge the tainted, starting with you as the snitch. Kagha is a trusted member of the grove and is clearly torn — her voice trembles and she may be persuadable, but convincing her to renounce the shadow teachings will be very difficult, especially if the child mentioned earlier was already killed. The scene forces a choice: try to sway Kagha away from the shadows (with strong roleplay checks), or fight Olodan and his newly transformed druids while Rath and other circle members react to the betrayal.
- DEN_ShadowDruid_LeaderPersuaded.json: You revealed Kagha to be a Shadow Druid, but convinced her to stand against them. She now contemplates what has happened, repentant and ready to stand trial for her crimes.

- Rath: This is madness, Kagha. She's just a... (node 237)
- Kagha: A what, Rath? A thief? A poison? A threat? (node 45)
- Kagha: Do it. (node 172)

context: The druids have convened a “court” to judge a tiefling child (Arabella) accused of stealing a precious grove artifact; a guardian snake coils at her side as she begs for mercy. You’ve already exposed Kagha as a Shadow Druid, and a Cloakwood contingent led by Olodan has arrived, warping grove creatures into shadow-druids and pressing the circle to purge anything “tainted.” Kagha is a trusted leader who is visibly torn but leaning toward harsh measures—labeling the child a thief/poison and threatening imprisonment or exile—while Rath argues in the child’s defense. If you fail to stop the purge, the child will try to run and the guardian snakes will attack, at which point Kagha can flip fully to a darker, more violent stance; alternatively you can attempt to sway Kagha or fight Olodan and his transformed druids.
